title: Accessibility basics: How to make your game more accessible
summary: Learn the basics of game accessibility: Where to begin, simple solutions for hearing, vision, motor, and cognitive needs, and why you should get started early.
body_markdown:
## Plan for accessibility early in video game design


The best time to make a video game accessible is at the start. Many basic capabilities are simple to add if you plan for them early. Retrofitting them at the end, after menus, controls, and effects are locked in, often causes messy and expensive reworks.


A practical approach is to add a few accessibility questions to your game plan from day one. Which information does your game communicate only through sound? Only through color? Which actions need fast or held inputs? Answering those early helps you design around barriers instead of patching them later.


## Make room for more players


Accessibility isn’t a feature you bolt on at the end. It’s a way of thinking about who gets to play. Start with the basics – controls, text, color, and subtitles – then keep asking where your game might shut someone out. Every barrier you remove is another person who gets to enjoy what you made.
